subject: RENEWAL: EU onshore partition + APAC warm-failover — cost allocation & SOW
messages:
From: Sara Keller <sara.keller@novaclinic.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: NovaClinic Procurement <procurement@novaclinic.com>
Date: 2028-08-30T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal & region expansion questions — EU onshore + APAC warm-failover

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the renewal notice. We're keen to move forward but have a few open items before the finance and legal teams will sign:

1) EU onshore residency: we need the SOW to explicitly call out a dedicated EU onshore tenancy for PII and audit logs, with defined data-at-rest boundaries.
2) APAC rollout: we want a staged APAC warm-failover (cold-to-warm standby) for US->EU primary traffic spikes. Sizing: initial pilot 50k reqs/day, scale to 250k within 6 months.
3) SLA & credits: after the intermittent latency incidents in June, procurement is asking for a modest credit line or service-rate reduction tied to uptime/95th latency for the new term.
4) Cost split and billing: because parts of this work are residency engineering + region capacity, we need clarity on how Redwood will apportion one-time onshore onboarding fees vs ongoing seats/throughput billing.

I've attached our SOW sketch (SOW_draft_v3.pdf) and a short incident summary (latency_incident_summary.xlsx) for context. Can your team share a short one-pager that maps changes in the renewal (term, seats, failover) to expected cost delta and the proposed credit escrow?

We'd like a call next week (Sep 4–6 window) to run through the mutual action plan. I can bring procurement if we have the rough numbers ahead of time.

Best,
Sara
Director of Engineering Programs
NovaClinic

--
Attachment(s): SOW_draft_v3.pdf (application/pdf), latency_incident_summary.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-09-01T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal & region expansion questions — EU onshore + APAC warm-failover

Sara — thanks for the clear asks and the attachments. We've reviewed and can propose a path that keeps the renewal timeline intact while addressing residency, rollout, and the credit request. High level: 

- EU onshore tenancy: Redwood can provision a customer-dedicated instance in our EU region with isolated storage and a controlled audit-log pipeline (SOC2 audit will reflect this environment). We will include a residency clause in the SOW with the data-at-rest boundary and audit access windows.

- APAC warm-failover plan: propose a 3-stage rollout — Pilot (50k req/day for 30 days) -> Warm Tier (150k req/day for 60 days) -> Scale (250k req/day steady). Warm-failover will use cross-region KV cache seeding and a hot-standby routing policy.

- SLA credit: we'll offer a renewal credit equal to one month of committed throughput if we miss committed 95th latency targets more than twice in a rolling 6-month window during the first 12 months post-onboarding. The credit is scoped to committed throughput only.

- Cost split: onboarding (one-time) fees for EU onshore setup and audit integration will be billed as Professional Services (PS). Ongoing throughput seats and burst capacity billed monthly. For the SOW we can present both a blended and a detailed line-item view; my recommendation is to show a blended uplift percent plus a PS line for EU onboarding so procurement can decide which to amortize.

Attached is the Redwood proposal and a one-page impact summary (redwood_proposal_eu_onshore_apac_warmstandby.pdf). Key dates:
  • Draft SOW review: Sep 5
  • Pilot start: Oct 2
  • Production cutover to warm-failover: Nov 15

Proposed next step: 45-minute call on Sep 5 to review the SOW pages and the credit mechanics. If that works, I will send a calendar invite and include legal for redlines.

Thanks — cc'ing Ben (sales lead) and Rishi (solutions/infra) to align on pricing and runbook.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

--
Attachment(s): redwood_proposal_eu_onshore_apac_warmstandby.pdf (application/pdf); One-pager summary included inline in the PDF.

Hannah — quick internal notes before the Sep 5 call: 

1) Pricing approach: recommend we present two commercial options on the call — \"Blended Uplift\" (single percent increase rolled into committed monthly spend) and \"PS + Throughput\" (separate PS line for EU onshore + incremental throughput seats). Blended is easier to sign; PS gives NovaClinic CAPEX transparency.

2) Credit mechanics: the proposed credit sounds fair but procurement will ask for clearer measurement instrumentation. Rishi, can we surface the token-level latency slices so procurement/legal can map credit triggers to measurable metrics?

3) Contract terms: Laura, please flag any clauses in the proposed SOW that might need explicit language around data egress limitations and audit access windows. Legal will push for max 30-day retention of raw audit exports unless otherwise approved.

4) Sales ask: do we want to offer an introductory month of reduced throughput pricing for the pilot (50% on pilot-month) to reduce friction? It would be funded from the renewal credit line if later triggered. Thoughts?

-ben
